beats.name: Exponential Inversion Hook
beats.text: Drop a standard sewing needle from your hand, and it hits the floor with barely enough energy to bend a blade of grass. But what if that same one-gram needle struck Earth at ninety-nine point nine-nine-nine-nine percent the speed of light?

beats.name: Perspective 1: Ground Reality
beats.text: If you were standing on the ground looking up, the sky would look completely peaceful. You wouldn't see a flaming meteor streak, and you wouldn't hear a screaming whistle. Because the needle travels at lightspeed, light only beats the projectile by a fraction of a nanosecond. You see nothing—until reality explodes.

beats.name: Perspective 2: Relativistic Simulator
beats.text: In the physics simulator, Einstein's equations take over. With a Lorentz factor of seven hundred, length contraction crushes the five-centimeter steel pin into a microscopic disc just seventy microns thick. Crossing the entire atmosphere in three hundred microseconds, it punches head-on through air molecules, boring a laser-thin fusion plasma tube straight to the ground.

beats.name: Crust Impact & Kinetic Dump
beats.text: The moment it touches solid rock, sixty-three trillion Joules of kinetic energy dump into the crust in nanoseconds. That is fifteen kilotons of TNT—the exact explosive yield of the Hiroshima atomic bomb—unleashed from a single gram of steel.

beats.name: Biological Takeaway
beats.text: A three-hundred-meter crater vaporizes in an instant, flattening the landscape for miles. And you would never even know it happened—because you would be gone faster than your optic nerve could send a single signal to your brain.
